newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai plane in emergency landing after fire signal.
newsitem.headline: Thai plane in emergency landing after fire signal.

text.p: A Thai Airways International airbus with 160 people on board was forced to make an emergency landing on Sunday night after a fire warning signal was triggered, an airline official said on Monday.

The airbus A3-600B flight bound for Kaula Lumpur was forced to return to the Bangkok airport 15 minutes after takeoff when, at an altitude of 7,000 feet, the pilot noticed the warning signal, a Thai Airways official told Reuters.
The captain switched off one of the two engines after the fire signal, the official said.
Witnesses told a radio station they saw a trail of fire from the left-wing engine before the plane turned around for its emergency landing.
However, the airline official denied reports that there had been a fire in the engine.
All passengers were safely evacuated from the plane and boarded another aircraft for Malaysia, the official said.
